question: Does the RAW local contrast rank one hypothesis (D6-prime) survive the same falsification search that kills the centred one (D6)?
design: Identical script, seed, corner, fibre count, optimizer, snapping and StrictTopC gate. The only difference is --fiber-kind. The centred arm is a POSITIVE CONTROL: it must find a violation, and it does, reproducing the recorded record B3small_m6_d16_s13 to the digit.
reading: Control KILLED at 1.1611; raw arm found no counterexample and topped out at 0.958515, below 1, at matched budget. First real evidence for D6-prime.
caveats: --snap both was used. The 'project' snapping branch can leave V^raw_phi, so some raw-arm leads may not have satisfied the hypothesis. This dilutes the search; it does not turn a null into a false null, but the clean run is --snap coefficients.

The exact recheck in this script verifies CENTRED rank one (exact_rankone_verified_count), not raw rank one. The raw arm's witnesses are in the fibre by construction of the basis, not by an independent certificate.
One corner (corner 0), one seed (13), one denominator (16), 24 fibres. A null at one budget point.
A per-fibre float search maximises a LOWER bound and is path dependent. This is evidence, never proof. D6-prime remains OPEN.
The raw arm topped out at 0.9585, only 4.3% under the bound. That is NOT a comfortable margin: a modest budget increase could still cross 1.
next: Replicate across seeds and denominators, as was done for the centred arm.
Rerun both arms with --snap coefficients so the raw arm's leads provably stay in the fibre.
Extend the exact recheck to verify raw rank one directly (raw contrast matrix rank <= 1 per coordinate).
